title: Interventions and plugins (Interrupts, human in the loop, and skills) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 04
summary: A deck for Python developers who have built a Strands Agents agent with tools and hooks, on how to put people and rules in the loop. It then shows how plugins bundle hooks and tools, how skills load their instructions only when needed, how intervention handlers return Proceed, Deny, or Guide, and how steering gives feedback in plain words. Every example is real code with its real output, run on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region with global cross-Region inference, with architecture diagrams and flow charts. The facts come from the official Strands Agents documentation only, and the examples use a help-desk agent with made-up customers and orders, made for this series. As of November 2026 (Strands Agents 1.64, Level 300). This is deck 04 (Go deeper) of the Learn Strands Agents with Kiro series.
ja_summary:
・Python開発者向けに、Strands AgentsでAIの判断に人間を介在させる制御技術（承認確認、ルール適用、中断・再開機能）を解説。

title: AI review (Reviewers by role, and what counts as blocking) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 05
summary: Level 300. An agent that grades its own work praises even mediocre work, so this deck splits the builder from a separate checker and shows what to give that checker: the change, the requirements, and the rules, not the author's reasons. On a small booking app, it builds Kiro reviewers by viewpoint, gives the builder and the checker the same grading criteria, applies rules only to the files they cover, defines a blocking finding by four parts, and measures a reviewer's misses and false alarms with four kinds of change. This is deck 05 (Check pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.
ja_summary:

title: Platform Engineering after the AI Hype: Why IDPs Must Become Intent-Driven
summary:
The first wave of platform engineering focused on Kubernetes abstraction: templates (Crossplane + OpenTofu), golden paths (Helm + Argo), and self-service APIs (often fronted by Backstage). Then AI coding agents arrived, and suddenly, platform building was a solved problem. Just add MCP, right? Maybe… actually, no.

Infrastructure requests are increasingly being generated by copilots, workflow agents, and automation systems operating at machine speed. Platform teams now need APIs and workflows designed for both humans and AI systems.

This talk explores how internal platforms must evolve from infrastructure-centric interfaces toward intent-driven platform capabilities that encode organisational policy, security, and operational knowledge.

Drawing on lessons from real-world platform implementations, we’ll examine the new failure modes AI introduces to platform engineering, why traditional abstraction layers break down, and how workflow-centric capabilities can scale effectively.
ja_summary:
AIによる自動化の進展により、従来のK8s抽象化を中心としたプラットフォーム構築手法は限界を迎えている。
今後は人間だけでなくAIからの要求も想定し、組織のポリシーや運用知見を組み込んだ「意図駆動型」への進化が不可欠となる。
AIがもたらす新たな故障モードを防ぎつつ、ワークフロー中心の機能へと転換することで、プラットフォームのスケーラビリティを確保する。
